A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite extensive renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original celebrity and explicit-content erasure experiments, including attack comparisons, ablations, training trajectories and multiple-trigger tests.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds data-poisoning, object-erasure, additional-model and defense-detection results.

M1.justification: V2 adds EEBdata, which establishes backdoors through poisoned image–text training pairs without attacker access to model weights. This substantially extends the three weight-based procedures. ToxETextEnc, ToxEX-Attn and ToxEDISA are renamed EEBsurface, EEBshallow and EEBdeep; their central mechanisms and the deep attack's three-loss objective are retained.

E1.justification: V2 adds object erasure using the ten CIFAR-10 categories and uses LAION-Aesthetics data for poisoned fine-tuning. The celebrity identities and 931 sexual-category I2P prompts remain. The additional SD v2.1 and FLUX configurations are model-setting changes rather than new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: ADVUNLEARN, merely cited in v1, becomes an evaluated defense in v2's main comparisons and multiple-trigger experiments. EEBdata also becomes an additional attack comparator. The five original erasure methods and three original weight-based attack variants remain, substantially expanding comparisons without treating renaming as new methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds CLIPScore, an object-classifier evaluation protocol, and SD v2.1/FLUX configurations. Appendix B changes the explicit-content deep-attack learning rate from 2e-5 to 5e-5. Explicit-content percentages now compare against the clean erased model, whereas v1 Table 9 compares triggered and untriggered outputs of each poisoned model. The larger amplification figures therefore do not establish same-setting gains.

E4.justification: V2 adds an alpha sensitivity analysis and WeightWatcher diagnostics testing whether poisoning leaves detectable weight changes. It extends erasure trajectories to EEBdata and ADVUNLEARN and multiple-trigger studies to ADVUNLEARN. Existing loss/template ablations remain, but v1's explicit-content trigger-sensitivity analysis and associated comparisons are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages across targets or triggers and display shaded trajectory curves. V2 adds no new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, defined confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results, including 80.16% celebrity ASR for EEBdata against RECE and 94.40% object ASR for EEBdeep against RECE. Shared celebrity results such as 82.48% deep-attack ASR against UCE remain unchanged. Explicit-content counts are replaced under revised settings, clean-model FID changes from 54.21 to 39.78, and most Acco entries and explicit-content trigger sweeps disappear. V2 Table 2's weight-based accuracies match single-trigger results already reported in v1 Table 5.

T1.justification: The deep attack's losses and combined objective in Equations 3–6, together with Appendix A's erasure formulations, retain their mathematical substance. V2 makes prompt-template notation explicit but adds no substantive theoretical derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central vulnerability claim expands from white-box attacks on SD v1.4 to black-box data poisoning and multiple architectures. V2 adds object-erasure claims, raises the headline explicit-content amplification from approximately 9-fold to 16-fold under revised comparisons, and explicitly presents EEB as a diagnostic tool for testing erasure robustness.

C2.justification: V1 attributes improved deep-attack FID partly to self-distillation; v2 instead describes weight-based attacks as largely preserving fidelity and discusses data-poisoning degradation. V2 adds interpretations concerning attack–defense component overlap and SD v2.1 target–trigger entanglement. It also specifies limitations involving incompatible defenses, preliminary FLUX testing, untested text-agnostic safety methods and clean-reference requirements for weight diagnostics.

D1.justification: V2 adds data-poisoning and ADVUNLEARN implementation settings plus Appendix F's GPU specifications and method runtimes. Conversely, Appendix G replaces the complete retention and training-template lists with examples and a future-release promise. The release plan now includes reviewer code and poisoned checkpoints, but their availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 broadens positioning toward practical data poisoning and text-agnostic safety alignment, adding discussions of Carlini et al., SafeGen, Direct Unlearning Optimization, SafetyDPO and ERASEFLOW. Several earlier general-background and self-distillation references are removed. The original distinction from work exploiting unlearning to implant backdoors remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, threat model and concluding discussion are substantially rewritten. Terminology changes throughout from ToxE/DISA to EEB and its variants. Trajectory analysis moves into the appendix, ablations are reorganized, and a separate Impact Statement is added. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: V2 introduces new overview diagrams, removes the DISA training diagram, expands qualitative grids and comparison tables, and adds object/model results and a weight-diagnostic plot. The trajectory grid is transposed and relocated. Appendices change to a single-column layout, while full template tables and additional qualitative grids are removed.

improvement.justification: The data-poisoning experiments and SD v2.1/FLUX tests substantially strengthen the threat's credibility beyond v1's direct-weight-access, single-backbone setting. Object erasure, ADVUNLEARN comparisons and sensitivity analysis further test applicability and design choices. These gains outweigh the loss of complete prompt/retention lists and untriggered poisoned-model controls, although those omissions weaken reproducibility and prevent direct comparison of the headline explicit-content amplification.
